parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just-cause eviction), as amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01; operative 2024-04-01, sunsets 2030-01-01. Requires just cause after 12 months, relocation assistance of one month's rent for no-fault terminations, with exemptions and deference to stricter local ordinances.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the landlord may only end the tenancy for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations, the landlord must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance (within 15 days of notice) or waive the final month's rent.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.effective_date_note: Section became operative April 1, 2024 per subdivision (m); amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01. Repealed as of 2030-01-01.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; relocation = 1 month's rent for no-fault
rules.penalty: Noncompliant termination notice is void; actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x damages for willful violations, plus punitive damages; AG/city attorney/county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; certain nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied (up to two rooms/units rented); owner-occupied duplex; housing with CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g., single-family homes/condos) owned by non-REIT/corp/LLC-with-corp-member owner with written exemption notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies where tenant has occupied 12+ months (or 24 months if additional adults added); does not apply where a local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or a later local ordinance that is more protective; a property is not subject to both.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property (single-family/condo) with non-corporate owner and exemption notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels
